claims: Shell model EC rates on pf-shell nuclei accurately reproduce charge-exchange GT+ data with a standard (0.74)^2 quenching.
20Ne ground-state to ground-state second-forbidden EC increases rates by orders of magnitude, shifting oxygen ignition off-center.
Multi-particle multi-hole correlations and thermal excitations unblock GT+ transitions across N=40 and N=50 shell gaps, proving heavy nuclei dominate EC throughout collapse.
First-forbidden transitions in N=126 r-process waiting points noticeably accelerate beta decay, enhancing mass flow toward fissioning nuclei and shaping the A~130 abundance peak.
SMMC level densities and low-energy M1 strength upbend/scissors mode significantly enhance statistical neutron capture rates in the r-process.
